subject: ophthalmology
title: Optic nerve disorders

steps.tx: **Papilloedema** means bilateral optic disc swelling from raised intracranial pressure caused by tumours, hydrocephalus, venous sinus thrombosis or **idiopathic intracranial hypertension**, which typically affects young obese women. Expect engorged veins, peripapillary haemorrhages, preserved early acuity and enlarged blind spots, with chronic cases fading to optic atrophy. Evaluate with brain imaging including venography, then measure opening pressure by lumbar puncture once a mass is excluded. **Foster Kennedy syndrome** pairs ipsilateral optic atrophy with contralateral disc swelling and localises a frontal lesion.
steps.say: Both optic discs look swollen in a patient with headache and vomiting, so you should suspect raised intracranial pressure and arrange brain imaging with venography. Idiopathic intracranial hypertension typically affects young obese women, and lumbar puncture confirms high opening pressure once imaging has excluded a mass. Chronic swelling fades into optic atrophy, so early treatment protects vision.

vis.alt: Fundus photograph showing severe bilateral optic disc swelling, blurred margins, engorged veins, and peripapillary hemorrhages, characteristic of acute papilloedema.

steps.tx: **Optic neuritis** linked to multiple sclerosis typically strikes young women with subacute unilateral vision loss, pain on eye movement, washed out colour vision and an afferent pupil defect, while the disc looks normal or mildly swollen because most cases are retrobulbar. Confirm demyelination with MRI of the brain and orbits, and give steroids to hasten recovery even though final acuity remains unchanged. **Neuromyelitis optica** causes severe bilateral attacks with longitudinal spinal cord inflammation and relapses aggressively, so plasma exchange and immunosuppression limit further episodes. MOG associated disease behaves similarly.
steps.say: Pain on eye movement with unilateral vision loss and washed out colours in a young woman points to optic neuritis, so arrange MRI of the brain and orbits to confirm demyelination. Steroids hasten recovery even though the final acuity remains unchanged. Severe bilateral attacks with spinal cord inflammation suggest neuromyelitis optica, which needs plasma exchange and continued immunosuppression.

steps.tx: This four panel MRI shows an **enhancing optic nerve lesion** on contrast enhanced T1 fat saturated coronal and axial images, marked by arrows along the swollen left optic nerve, which confirms active inflammation in **optic neuritis**. The axial and sagittal FLAIR panels show bright **demyelinating plaques** scattered around the ventricles and corpus callosum, which establish dissemination in space for **multiple sclerosis**. Recognising this combination helps you link painful vision loss with demyelination in the exam.
steps.say: The top two panels show a bright enhancing lesion along the swollen optic nerve on contrast images, which confirms active inflammation in optic neuritis. The lower FLAIR panels show bright demyelinating plaques around the ventricles and corpus callosum, which point to multiple sclerosis. When painful vision loss comes with these plaques, you can confidently link the eye presentation to demyelinating disease.

steps.tx: **Nonarteritic ischaemic optic neuropathy** strikes elderly vasculopaths who wake with a painless altitudinal field cut on a crowded small disc, so control vascular risk factors and counsel about precipitants after the event. **Arteritic ischaemic optic neuropathy** from giant cell arteritis shows scalp tenderness, jaw claudication, raised inflammatory markers and a chalky pale disc, and it demands immediate high dose steroids to save the fellow eye before temporal artery biopsy. Posterior ischaemic variants can follow prolonged hypotension during major surgery and may affect both eyes.
steps.say: An elderly patient who wakes with a painless half field cut on a crowded disc has nonarteritic ischaemia, so control vascular risk factors and counsel about precipitants. Scalp tenderness with jaw pain and a chalky pale disc means arteritic disease, which needs immediate high dose steroids to save the other eye before biopsy. Posterior variants can follow prolonged low pressure during major surgery.

steps.tx: **Leber hereditary optic neuropathy** causes painless sequential central scotomas in young men through mitochondrial inheritance, with circumpapillary telangiectasia in the acute phase, so counsel about maternal transmission and smoking avoidance. **Dominant optic atrophy** produces insidious temporal pallor and needs family screening. **Compressive optic neuropathy** from pituitary adenoma, meningioma or aneurysm progresses slowly with field cuts, often bitemporal, respecting the vertical meridian and optic pallor, so arrange MRI with endocrine review before surgery. Toxic and nutritional causes improve after withdrawing the agent and replacing deficiency.
steps.say: Sequential painless central scotomas in a young man suggest Leber hereditary disease, so explain maternal inheritance and advise strict smoking avoidance. Insidious temporal pallor with a family history points to dominant optic atrophy, which needs screening of relatives. Slowly progressive field cuts respecting the vertical meridian mean compression, so arrange MRI with endocrine review before surgery.
